title: You are the true Creator
hook: too kartaa sachiaar maiddaa saanee: You are the true Creator, my Master (Asa M4, ang 11)
tomorrow: A pool of fire and water

segments.voice: Yesterday, So Purakh, and your line, pure being. Did you see a flame and remember niranjan? Today, Guru Ram Das's second shabad, and it speaks straight to the Maker. Day four hundred ten.

Pick up a handmade bowl at a craft fair and turn it over. On the bottom, pressed into the clay, there's often a little mark: initials, a symbol, the potter's stamp. The bowl doesn't know it's there. It just holds soup. But the mark says someone shaped this, on purpose, with their hands. Guru Ram Das looks at a whole day that way: the light this morning, the people in it, the breath you're breathing now. Tonight's shabad turns the day over and reads the mark. Today: You are the true Creator.

segments.voice: The second So Purakh shabad, by Guru Ram Das, opens: too kartaa sachiaar maiddaa saanee. You are the true Creator, my Master. Kartaa is the maker, the same word as in the Mool Mantar's karta purakh. Sachiaar is true. And maiddaa saanee, my Master, is said in western Punjabi forms, the speech of the plains around Multan, so even the grammar sounds like someone talking at home. Then, in paraphrase: whatever pleases You comes to pass; whatever You give, that is what I receive. All belongs to You, and all meditate on You. The one You bless receives the jewel of the Name. The shabad gives the two directions a person can face: the gurmukh, turned toward the Guru, finds it; the manmukh, turned toward the self, loses it. Then come two pictures. You Yourself separate us, the shabad says, and You Yourself bring us together. And: You are the river, and everything is within You; without You, there is no other. All beings are Your play. So the Maker isn't standing outside the day, like a potter who walked away from the wheel. The Maker is the river the whole day flows in. For Sikhs saying Rehras, that changes what thank you means at dusk: not thanks sent off to a distant address, but the bowl noticing the hands still holding it. And the closing note is trust, said simply: You are my Master.
screen: `TOO KARTAA SACHIAAR: YOU ARE THE TRUE MAKER.` · `WHAT YOU GIVE IS WHAT I RECEIVE.` · `GURMUKH FINDS, MANMUKH LOSES.` · `YOU ARE THE RIVER; ALL IS IN YOU.` · then, large: `MY MASTER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: thank the maker of your day. Turn today over, like the bowl, and look underneath. Find three things you didn't make yourself: the morning light, someone who cooked or drove or helped, the breath itself. Let each one come to mind slowly. For each, a quiet thank you. If you pray, you can say the shabad's own words, too kartaa sachiaar maiddaa saanee, or simply Waheguru. Then rest. The bell holds the time.
You are the true Creator. Too kartaa sachiaar maiddaa saanee: Guru Ram Das calls the Lord the true Maker and his Master, the river in which everything flows.
screen: `YOU ARE THE TRUE CREATOR — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: my master. Today, when something arrives that you didn't plan, good or hard, try saying inside: what You give, I receive. Day four hundred ten.

howItsDone: Too kartaa sachiaar is the second shabad of the So Purakh group in Rehras Sahib, recited each evening; its line that the Lord is the river within which all things are is often quoted in Sikh teaching.

fork.setup: Guru Ram Das gives a picture of how the Maker relates to everything made. which is it?
options: a potter who has left the wheel.
the river, with everything within it.
a king far off in a palace.
fork.reveal: You are the river, and everything is within You; without You there is no other.

original.note: Gurmukhi: kartaa, the Maker; as in the Mool Mantar's karta purakh.

trapdoor: what you thought: You are the true Creator is a standard title of praise.
what it means: the Maker isn't outside the day but the river it flows in; what is given is received with trust.
what a scholar hears: maiddaa and saanee are Lahnda (western Punjabi) forms, part of the many regional registers in the Guru Granth Sahib's language.

sources.ref: Asa M4, too kartaa sachiaar maiddaa saanee, Ang 11

notes: Shabad paraphrased: You are the true Creator, my Master; what pleases You happens, what You give I receive; all is Yours; the one You bless gets the jewel of the Name; gurmukh finds, manmukh loses; You separate and unite; You are the river, all within You; all beings Your play. Confirm.
Maiddaa/saanee as Lahnda (western Punjabi, Multani) forms: confirm.
Audit (2026-10-01): the hook stated as the narrator's own fact that 'somebody made your day'; it now attributes that view to Guru Ram Das and the shabad. Trimmed a doubled closing line.
